quests.instruction: Identify the nature event where the Sun's warmth turns water into invisible vapor in the air!
quests.question: Evaporation
quests.hint: Puddles slowly disappear on a sunny day because of this invisible process.
quests.explanation: Yes! Evaporation is correct because it is when the Sun's warmth turns water into invisible vapor.
quests.funFact: Evaporation is the very first step of the whole water cycle!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event where invisible water vapor cools down and turns back into tiny water droplets!
quests.question: Condensation
quests.hint: This is exactly how a cold glass of lemonade gets droplets on the outside.
quests.explanation: Yes! Condensation is correct because it is when water vapor cools and turns back into tiny droplets.
quests.funFact: Condensation is exactly how clouds form high up in the sky!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event that describes any water falling from the sky, like rain, snow, or hail!
quests.question: Precipitation
quests.hint: This is the science word for water falling down to the ground from the clouds above.
quests.explanation: Yes! Precipitation is correct because it describes any water falling from the sky, like rain or snow.
quests.funFact: Precipitation can fall as rain, snow, sleet, or hail, depending on the temperature!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event where a plant's leaves use sunlight to make their own food!
quests.question: Photosynthesis
quests.hint: This is why a plant's leaves always try to reach toward the light.
quests.explanation: Yes! Photosynthesis is correct because it is when a plant's leaves use sunlight to make their own food.
quests.funFact: Photosynthesis also releases the very oxygen that people and animals need to breathe!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event where pollen moves from one flower to another, helping make new seeds!
quests.question: Pollination
quests.hint: Bees and butterflies carry this tiny yellow dust from flower to flower without even trying.
quests.explanation: Yes! Pollination is correct because it is when pollen moves between flowers, helping make new seeds.
quests.funFact: About one third of all the food we eat exists because of pollination!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event where a tiny seed cracks open and begins to grow into a plant!
quests.question: Germination
quests.hint: Warmth, water, and a little bit of soil are all this sleepy seed needs to wake up.
quests.explanation: Yes! Germination is correct because it is when a tiny seed cracks open and begins to grow.
quests.funFact: Some seeds can stay asleep in the soil for years before germination finally begins!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event where a plant releases water vapor into the air through its leaves!
quests.question: Transpiration
quests.hint: This is a little like how a plant quietly 'breathes out' extra water all day long.
quests.explanation: Yes! Transpiration is correct because it is when a plant releases water vapor through its leaves.
quests.funFact: A single large tree can release hundreds of liters of water into the air through transpiration every day!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event where rock slowly breaks down into smaller pieces right where it sits!
quests.question: Weathering
quests.hint: Wind, rain, ice, and even plant roots can slowly crack rock apart over time.
quests.explanation: Yes! Weathering is correct because it is when rock slowly breaks into smaller pieces right where it sits.
quests.funFact: Weathering happens in place, while erosion is what carries the broken pieces away afterward!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that is all the living and non-living things working together in one place!
quests.question: Ecosystem
quests.hint: Plants, animals, soil, water, and weather all connect together to make up this whole system.
quests.explanation: Yes! An Ecosystem is correct because it is all the living and non-living things working together in one place.
quests.funFact: A single drop of pond water can actually be its own tiny ecosystem, full of life!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event where water travels from the sea, into the sky, and back down again!
quests.question: Water Cycle
quests.hint: This never-ending journey includes evaporation, clouds forming, and rain falling back down.
quests.explanation: Yes! The Water Cycle is correct because it is water's endless journey from the sea, to the sky, and back.
quests.funFact: The exact same water has been cycling around our planet for billions of years!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event that makes a wet sidewalk dry off after the rain stops!
quests.question: Evaporation
quests.hint: Warm air quietly lifts tiny bits of water up into the sky, out of sight.
quests.explanation: That's right! Evaporation is correct because warm air lifts water up into the sky, drying the sidewalk.
quests.funFact: The ocean loses a huge amount of water to evaporation every single day!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event that forms clouds when rising water vapor finally cools down!
quests.question: Condensation
quests.hint: Millions of these tiny water droplets clump together to form a fluffy cloud.
quests.explanation: That's right! Condensation is correct because it forms clouds as rising water vapor cools down.
quests.funFact: The same process that makes clouds also makes fog form close to the ground!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event where clouds finally release their water back down to Earth!
quests.question: Precipitation
quests.hint: This can happen gently as a drizzle, or heavily as a downpour.
quests.explanation: That's right! Precipitation is correct because it is when clouds release their water back down to Earth.
quests.funFact: Some deserts barely get any precipitation at all for years at a time!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event where green leaves turn sunlight, water, and air into energy for a plant!
quests.question: Photosynthesis
quests.hint: A plant's green color comes from the very same part that makes this process possible.
quests.explanation: That's right! Photosynthesis is correct because green leaves turn sunlight, water, and air into energy.
quests.funFact: Without photosynthesis, there would be no food chain for any plant or animal to depend on!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event that happens when a bee brushes against pollen while drinking nectar!
quests.question: Pollination
quests.hint: The bee doesn't mean to help, but it carries tiny grains of this to the next flower it visits.
quests.explanation: That's right! Pollination is correct because a bee carries pollen to the next flower while collecting nectar.
quests.funFact: Wind can also cause pollination, carrying pollen between flowers without any help from insects!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event that happens just before a tiny sprout pushes up through the soil!
quests.question: Germination
quests.hint: This is the very moment a resting seed wakes up and starts its journey into a plant.
quests.explanation: That's right! Germination is correct because it happens just before a sprout pushes up through the soil.
quests.funFact: Gardeners often soak seeds in water first to help germination begin a little faster!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event that helps pull water all the way up from a plant's roots to its leaves!
quests.question: Transpiration
quests.hint: As water leaves through the top of a plant, more gets pulled up from the roots below.
quests.explanation: That's right! Transpiration is correct because it helps pull water up from the roots to the leaves.
quests.funFact: On a hot day, a forest full of trees can add a huge amount of moisture to the air through transpiration!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event that slowly crumbles a mountain's rock, little by little, over centuries!
quests.question: Weathering
quests.hint: Freezing water can seep into tiny cracks in rock and slowly force them wider apart.
quests.explanation: That's right! Weathering is correct because it slowly crumbles rock, little by little, over centuries.
quests.funFact: Even the hardest rock on Earth eventually crumbles apart from years of weathering!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object where plants, animals, and their surroundings all depend on one another!
quests.question: Ecosystem
quests.hint: If just one part of this connected system changes, everything else can be affected too.
quests.explanation: That's right! An Ecosystem is correct because plants, animals, and their surroundings all depend on each other.
quests.funFact: A forest, a coral reef, and a desert are each their own completely different ecosystem!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event made up of evaporation, condensation, and precipitation happening again and again!
quests.question: Water Cycle
quests.hint: This constant loop never stops circulating around our entire planet.
quests.explanation: That's right! The Water Cycle is correct because it repeats evaporation, condensation, and precipitation endlessly.
quests.funFact: Without the water cycle, rain would never refill rivers, lakes, or oceans!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event where liquid water quietly turns into gas and rises into the sky!
quests.question: Evaporation
quests.hint: You can't see this happening, but it's why a wet towel eventually feels dry.
quests.explanation: Great job! Evaporation is correct because liquid water turns into gas and rises into the sky.
quests.funFact: Faster-moving, warmer water evaporates more quickly than cold, still water!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event where you can see your breath turn into a tiny cloud on a cold day!
quests.question: Condensation
quests.hint: Warm, moist air from your breath suddenly cools in the cold air outside.
quests.explanation: Great choice! Condensation is correct because your warm breath cools and turns into a tiny visible cloud.
quests.funFact: Dew on the morning grass forms the exact same way, as air cools overnight!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event that fills rivers, lakes, and reservoirs with fresh water!
quests.question: Precipitation
quests.hint: Without this falling water, rivers and lakes would eventually run dry.
quests.explanation: Great job! Precipitation is correct because it fills rivers, lakes, and reservoirs with fresh water.
quests.funFact: Some rainforests receive more precipitation in one year than many deserts get in a whole decade!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event that only happens in a plant's leaves whenever sunlight is shining!
quests.question: Photosynthesis
quests.hint: This is the reason plants need sunshine just as much as they need water.
quests.explanation: Great choice! Photosynthesis is correct because it only happens in a plant's leaves whenever sunlight shines.
quests.funFact: Scientists are still trying to build machines that can copy how well plants do photosynthesis!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event that must happen before most flowers can grow fruit or new seeds!
quests.question: Pollination
quests.hint: Without this tiny yellow dust traveling between flowers, many plants couldn't reproduce at all.
quests.explanation: Great job! Pollination is correct because it must happen before most flowers can grow fruit or seeds.
quests.funFact: Some flowers have bright colors and sweet smells purely to attract help with pollination!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event where water and warmth wake a sleeping seed up to start growing!
quests.question: Germination
quests.hint: Without the right amount of water and warmth, this seed would simply stay asleep.
quests.explanation: Great choice! Germination is correct because water and warmth wake a sleeping seed up to start growing.
quests.funFact: Not every seed that germinates will survive to become a full-grown plant!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event that adds invisible moisture to the air above a forest or field!
quests.question: Transpiration
quests.hint: This is one reason the air near lots of plants can feel a little more humid.
quests.explanation: Great job! Transpiration is correct because it adds invisible moisture to the air above plants.
quests.funFact: Transpiration plays a big part in forming the rain clouds above a thick rainforest!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event caused by wind, rain, and ice slowly wearing down solid rock over time!
quests.question: Weathering
quests.hint: This process happens so slowly that you'd never notice it happening in a single day.
quests.explanation: Great choice! Weathering is correct because wind, rain, and ice slowly wear down solid rock over time.
quests.funFact: Plant roots growing into cracks are a surprisingly powerful cause of weathering too!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object made up of a community of living things and the environment they share!
quests.question: Ecosystem
quests.hint: This whole connected community relies on sunlight, water, and soil to keep working.
quests.explanation: Great job! An Ecosystem is correct because it is a community of living things and the environment they share.
quests.funFact: Even a small backyard garden can be considered its very own little ecosystem!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event that explains how the same raindrop can fall again and again over millions of years!
quests.question: Water Cycle
quests.hint: This endless loop connects the sky, the land, and the sea, over and over again.
quests.explanation: Great choice! The Water Cycle is correct because it explains how the same water keeps moving in an endless loop.
quests.funFact: A single water molecule might spend thousands of years in the ocean before evaporating again!
